To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
severity of illness is the main determinant of cost variations in AMI patients.
severity of illness is a significant predictor of costs of acute medical care for AMI patients.

the DRG classification is not a good predictor of medical costs of acute myocardial care for the AMI patients, that severity of cardiac and cardiovascular illness as defined and operationalized is an excellent predictor, that the costs of acute medical care are mainly determined by the costs of thrombolytic treatment, CCU nursing care, cardiac catheterisation and PTCA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a method of severity adjustment for the purpose of cost analysis.
the development and application of a severity index for the diagnosis of acute myocardial ischemia, and with its use for explaining variations in the costs of medical care.

the following issues: 1) the relationship between the severity of cardiac and cardiovascular disorder and the costs of acute myocardial care; 2) the relationship between length of stay and costs of medical treatment; and 3) the relationship between severity of cardiac and vascular disorder and the costs for intensive nursing at the CCU.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the severity of illness of patients with acute myocardial infarcation is a major determinant of costs of medical care, but that the DRG classification is not the optimal way to measure the severity of illness.
severity of illness measured in terms of the severity of the cardiac disorders is the most relevant factor explaining the variations in costs of medical care of AMI patients.
the DRG classification is a useful and efficient instrument to predict cost variations in AMI, but the classification should be supplemented by severity of illness criteria.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the severity of illness of AMI patients is an important determinant of the costs of medical care.
the severity of illness of AMI patients has a strong impact on costs of medical care.
the severity of illness, as defined and measured in this study, explains a substantial part of the variations in costs for AMI patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the severity of illness is an important determinant of the cost of medical care in AMI patients.
severity of illness, as measured by the clinical criteria, is an important determinant of the costs of medical care.
the costs of medical care of AMI patients can be better predicted using clinical information than using the DRG classification.
